behavior: Highly social and often nomadic, forming large flocks outside the breeding season and moving in response to water availability and food supply; feeds by dabbling and up-ending in shallow water to reach submerged vegetation; forms strong monogamous pair bonds, with both sexes sharing incubation and cygnet care; known for elaborate paired courtship displays involving synchronized calling and neck movements.
field_marks: Almost entirely black plumage with curly, ruffled feathers on the back and wings
Bright red bill with a pale white-to-pinkish band near the tip
White flight feathers visible mainly in flight, contrasting with black body
Long, gracefully curved neck, longer relative to body than other swans
Legs and feet dark grey to black
habitat: Large shallow wetlands, lakes, swamps, estuaries, and slow-moving rivers with open water and abundant aquatic vegetation; also found in coastal lagoons and man-made reservoirs.
